sections.title: Opening the studio
body: Switch the vent fan on before anything else, then check the kiln room is above 10 °C: cold shelves crack.
Read yesterday's firing log and note any cone that bent short.

sections.title: Mixing glazes
body: Weigh dry materials to the gram, add water to a cream consistency and sieve twice.
Label every bucket with the recipe, the date and your initials.

sections.title: Loading the kiln
body: Wipe glaze off every foot. Leave a finger's width between pots and keep the cone pack visible from the spy hole.
Load heavy pieces low and the thin porcelain on the top shelf.

sections.title: Firing and cooling
body: Fire on the medium-speed schedule to cone 6 with a ten-minute hold, then let it cool closed.
Open below 100 °C. Crackle in a celadon keeps forming for days; that is the glaze, not a fault.

sections.title: Firing log
body: One line per firing: date, schedule, cone result and what came out wrong.
Keep it next to the kiln, not on a phone.
